scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Pas de quatre originated in the classical ballet tradition as a dance for four performers.
During the nineteenth century, its classical structure solidified around an entrée, solo variations, and a coda.

Jules Perrot established the benchmark in 1845 with his London work for four leading Romantic ballerinas, and Marius Petipa and Lev Ivanov further cemented the format in late-nineteenth-century Russian classical repertory.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Pas de quatre are usually plotless dances performed as divertissements to display technique and artistry within larger ballets.
However, narrative works also exist, such as José Limón's The Moor's Pavane, which interprets Shakespeare's Othello, and Antony Tudor's Jardin aux Lilas, which explores emotional entanglements.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: In standard classical structure, the pas de quatre begins with an entrée, transitions into individual variations for each dancer, and finishes with a shared coda.
In Lev Ivanov's 1895 Danse des petits cygnes, the four dancers perform with cross-linked hands, executing precise and dazzling footwork in strict synchronization.
Combinations can be all-female, all-male, or mixed ensembles.
Watch for Danse des petits cygnes linked line, Entrée, variations, and coda.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Major compositions associated with the format include Cesare Pugni's 1845 score for Perrot, Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky's music for Swan Lake (1895), Alexander Glazunov's score for Raymonda (1898), Ernest Chausson's music for Jardin aux Lilas (1936), Henry Purcell's music for The Moor's Pavane (1949), Igor Stravinsky's score for Agon (1957), and Giuseppe Verdi's music for Kenneth MacMillan's The Four Seasons (1975).
Listen for the orchestra.

The music spans Romantic, late-nineteenth-century Russian imperial, and twentieth-century neoclassical orchestral styles. Built around formal sections including an opening entrée, character variations, and an accelerating coda, the music provides clear metric support for athletic displays, lyricism, and synchronized footwork.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Key choreographers include Jules Perrot, Lev Ivanov, Marius Petipa, Antony Tudor, José Limón, George Balanchine, and Kenneth MacMillan.

Notable original performers include Marie Taglioni, Carlotta Grisi, Fanny Cerrito, Lucile Grahn, Sergei Legat, Georgi Kyasht, Nikolai Legat, Alexander Gorsky, Maude Lloyd, Hugh Laing, Peggy van Praagh, Betty Jones, Lucas Hoving, Pauline Koner, Lesley Collier, Michael Coleman, David Ashmole, and Wayne Eagling.

The pas de quatre has appeared across European, Russian, and American ballet traditions, with adaptations ranging from the French classical divertissement and British dramatic ballet to American neoclassical works and modern dance pavanes.
The pas de quatre developed directly from the structure of the classical pas de deux, expanding the architecture of entrée, variations, and coda to accommodate four dancers.
